gloss: to slip out; to stand out

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {抜|ぬ}け{出|で}ていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to slip out, to sneak out, to escape
definitions.explanation: To leave a place quietly or without being noticed, or to escape from a situation or confinement.

definitions.gloss: to stand out, to surpass, to excel
definitions.explanation: To be noticeably superior to others in ability, appearance, or quality. To rise above the group.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}をこっそり{抜|ぬ}け{出|で}た。
examples.english: I quietly slipped out of the meeting.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}が{家|いえ}を{抜|ぬ}け{出|で}て{遊|あそ}びに{行|い}った。
examples.english: The child snuck out of the house to go play.

examples.japanese: トンネルを{抜|ぬ}け{出|で}ると、{美|うつく}しい{景色|けしき}が{広|ひろ}がっていた。
examples.english: When I emerged from the tunnel, a beautiful landscape spread before me.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{群|ぐん}を{抜|ぬ}けて{美|うつく}しい。
examples.notes: The set phrase {群|ぐん}を{抜|ぬ}く/{抜|ぬ}けて means "to stand head and shoulders above the rest."

examples.japanese: {実力|じつりょく}が{抜|ぬ}け{出|で}ている{選手|せんしゅ}だ。
あのチームは{今季|こんき}、{他|ほか}を{大|おお}きく{引|ひ}き{離|はな}して{抜|ぬ}け{出|で}ている。
examples.english: That team has pulled far ahead of the others this season.

notes:
Ichidan verb ({一段動詞|いちだんどうし}).
- Negative: {抜|ぬ}け{出|で}ない
- Polite: {抜|ぬ}け{出|で}ます
- Te-form: {抜|ぬ}け{出|で}て
- Past: {抜|ぬ}け{出|で}た

USAGE:
In sense 1, the word implies stealth or an unnoticed departure. In sense 2, it emphasizes being clearly superior. The related compound verb {抜|ぬ}け{出|だ}す is sometimes used interchangeably for sense 1 (escaping), but {抜|ぬ}け{出|で}る is more standard.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- こっそり{抜|ぬ}け{出|で}る: to sneak out quietly
- {群|ぐん}を{抜|ぬ}けて: standing out from the crowd
- {渋滞|じゅうたい}を{抜|ぬ}け{出|で}る: to get out of a traffic jam
- {不況|ふきょう}から{抜|ぬ}け{出|で}る: to emerge from a recession
